title: SASSA Foster Child Grant 2026: Eligibility, Amount & Application Guide
description: Your guide to the SASSA Foster Child Grant (R1,290/month). Court order requirements, who qualifies, required documents, payment amounts, and key differences from the Child Support Grant.
author: Lucky Cungwa

sections.title: What is the SASSA Foster Child Grant?
sections.content: The SASSA Foster Child Grant is a monthly payment to foster parents who are caring for a child placed in their care by a children's court. As of 2026, the grant amount is {{foster_child_grant_amount}} per child per month, which is significantly higher than the Child Support Grant because it is intended to cover the full cost of caring for a child who cannot live with their biological parents. Unlike other grants, the Foster Child Grant is not means-tested in the same way — foster parents can receive it regardless of their income.

sections.title: Eligibility Requirements
sections.content:
To qualify for the SASSA Foster Child Grant in 2026, you must meet the following requirements:
  • Foster parent status: You must be a foster parent appointed by a children's court. A valid court order is required.
  • Child in care: The child must be under 18 years old and placed in your care by the court.
  • Citizenship: You and the child must be South African citizens or permanent residents.
  • No means test: Unlike other grants, there is no income or asset limit for foster parents. You can receive this grant regardless of your income.
  • Court order: An original or certified copy of the children's court order placing the child in your care is required.

sections.title: Difference Between Foster Child Grant and Child Support Grant
sections.content:
Many people confuse the Foster Child Grant with the Child Support Grant, but they are different:
  • Amount: Foster Child Grant is {{foster_child_grant_amount}} per month vs Child Support Grant at {{child_support_grant_amount}} per month.
  • Eligibility: Foster Child Grant requires a court order; Child Support Grant requires you to be the primary caregiver.
  • Means test: Foster Child Grant has no income limit; Child Support Grant has a means test.
  • Duration: Foster Child Grant is awarded for 2 years at a time; Child Support Grant continues until the child turns 18.
You cannot receive both grants for the same child.

sections.title: Required Documents
sections.content:
You need the following to apply for the Foster Child Grant:
  • Your 13-digit ID (green ID book or smart ID card)
  • Foster child's birth certificate (unabridged)
  • Children's court order (original or certified copy) placing the child in your foster care
  • Proof of residence — utility bill or affidavit
  • Social worker's report (if required by SASSA)

steps.title: Obtain a Children's Court Order
steps.content: Before you can apply for the grant, you must have a valid court order placing the child in your foster care. This involves going through the children's court process with the help of a social worker.

steps.title: Visit a SASSA Office
steps.content: Take the court order and all supporting documents to your nearest SASSA office.

steps.title: Submit the Application
steps.content: Complete the application form with the help of a SASSA officer. Both you and the child may need to be present.

steps.title: Receive Your Receipt
steps.content: You will receive a receipt with a reference number. Keep it as proof of your application.

steps.title: Grant is Awarded
steps.content: Once approved, you will receive payments from the date of application. Back pay is not paid for periods before your application date.

sections.title: Payment Dates & Amounts 2026
sections.content: The Foster Child Grant amount is {{foster_child_grant_amount}} per child per month in 2026. Payments are usually made from the 6th of each month. The grant is awarded for 2 years at a time, after which it must be reviewed and extended by the children's court. You can receive the grant for multiple foster children in your care.

faqs.q: Do I have to be related to the child to be a foster parent?
faqs.a: No. Foster parents do not need to be related to the child. Many foster parents are relatives (grandparents, aunts, uncles), but unrelated foster parents are also common.

faqs.q: Can I get both the Foster Child Grant and Child Support Grant?
faqs.a: No, you cannot receive both grants for the same child. If a child is in foster care, the Foster Child Grant is the correct grant.

faqs.q: What happens when the foster child turns 18?
faqs.a: The court order usually expires when the child turns 18. The grant will stop unless the court extends the foster care order.

faqs.q: Is the foster parent's income checked?
faqs.a: No, the Foster Child Grant does not have a means test. You can receive the grant regardless of your income level.
